title: A radiomics-based machine learning model and SHAP for predicting spread through air spaces and its prognostic implications in stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a multicenter cohort study.
summary: An elastic-net radiomics model selected from 15 machine-learning methods used preoperative CT tumor and peritumoral features to predict spread through air spaces in 609 stage-I lung-adenocarcinoma patients from three centers.
ai_technology: A multicentre radiomics model predicted spread through air spaces and prognosis in stage-I lung adenocarcinoma.

evidence.tested: Radiomics AUCs were 0.791 in training and 0.829/0.807 in two external tests; a combined clinical-imaging model reached 0.894 in one external set, while predicted or confirmed spread was associated with shorter progression-free survival. Prospective validation remains needed.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed source does not establish prospective benefit, broad external validity, or replication beyond the reported study.
evidence.ai_role: A multicentre radiomics model predicted spread through air spaces and prognosis in stage-I lung adenocarcinoma.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
